note: 英文原话来自 silicon-valley.tech，中文为本站 AI 翻译（以英文为准）

items.text_en: I think the Internet is the super-set of all media. It is the be-all and the end-all of all media. One will see print, broadcast, arguably, radio, essentially all media folding into the Internet.
items.text_zh: 我认为互联网是所有媒体的超集。它是一切媒体的终极归宿。人们会看到印刷、广播，可以说还有电台，基本上所有媒体都融入互联网之中。
items.source: Interview with Rita Braver, CBS Sunday Morning (1998), republished by CBS as "1998: Elon Musk on his early Silicon Valley days, future of the internet" (12 December 2022)

items.text_en: If things aren't not failing you are not innovating enough.
items.text_zh: 如果事情没有失败，说明你创新得还不够。
items.source: Fast Company, article "Hondas in Space" (1 February 2005)

items.text_en: I didn’t really expect to make any money. If I could make enough to cover the rent and buy some food that would be fine. As it turns out, it turned out to be quite valuable in the end.
items.text_zh: 我其实没指望赚什么钱。只要能赚够付房租、买点吃的就行了。结果到最后，它变得相当有价值。
items.source: The Wired Entrepreneur: The Early Years of Elon Musk', 2007.

items.text_en: I don’t have an issue with serving in the military per se, but serving in the South African army suppressing black people just didn’t seem like a really good way to spend time.
items.text_zh: 我本身并不反对服兵役，但在南非军队里服役、去镇压黑人，这看起来实在不是个度过时间的好办法。
items.source: The Wired Entrepreneur: The Early Years of Elon Musk', 2007.

items.text_en: I think South Africa is a great country.
items.text_zh: 我认为南非是个伟大的国家。
items.source: The Wired Entrepreneur: The Early Years of Elon Musk', 2007.

items.text_en: If you wanted to be close to the cutting edge, particularly in technology, you came to North America.
items.text_zh: 如果你想靠近最前沿，尤其是在技术领域，你就得来北美。
items.source: The Wired Entrepreneur: The Early Years of Elon Musk', 2007.

items.text_en: Tuition costs are outrageous. Fortunately, they gave me a scholarship…so I only had to cover living expenses, books, etc., by working.
items.text_zh: 学费高得离谱。幸运的是，他们给了我奖学金……所以我只需要靠打工来支付生活费、书本费等。
items.source: The Wired Entrepreneur: The Early Years of Elon Musk', 2007.

items.text_en: One was the Internet, one was clean energy and one was space.
items.text_zh: 一个是互联网，一个是清洁能源，一个是太空。
items.source: The Wired Entrepreneur: The Early Years of Elon Musk', 2007.

items.text_en: I could either watch it happen, or be part of it.
items.text_zh: 我可以选择旁观它发生，也可以选择成为它的一部分。
items.source: Zipping Forward: Musk Starts His First Company', 2007.

items.text_en: We could figure out ways with small aerospace companies to do a low-cost spacecraft and lander. But we could not find a way to do a low-cost launcher, unless we went to the Russians.
items.text_zh: 我们可以想办法和小型航空航天公司一起做低成本的航天器和着陆器。但我们找不到做低成本运载火箭的办法，除非去找俄罗斯人。
items.source: Lesson #1: Keep Your Operations Lean And Clean', 2007.

items.text_en: The answer was we thought it could be done.
items.text_zh: 答案是：我们认为这件事能做到。
items.source: Lesson #1: Keep Your Operations Lean And Clean', 2007.

items.text_en: There is nothing inherently expensive about rockets. It's just that those who have built and operated them in the past have done so with horrendously poor efficiency.
items.text_zh: 火箭本身并没有什么必然昂贵的地方。只是过去那些建造和运营火箭的人，效率低得可怕。
items.source: Lesson #1: Keep Your Operations Lean And Clean', 2007.

items.text_en: Falcon One is going to be the lowest cost per flight to orbit of any production rocket.
items.text_zh: Falcon One 将成为所有量产火箭中每次入轨飞行成本最低的。
items.source: Lesson #1: Keep Your Operations Lean And Clean', 2007.

items.text_en: Which means we’re cheaper than the Chinese, cheaper than [the] Russians or anywhere else – and we’re doing it in the United States with American labour costs.
items.text_zh: 这意味着我们的成本比中国低，比俄罗斯或任何其他地方都低——而且我们是在美国、用美国的劳动力成本做到这一点。
items.source: Lesson #1: Keep Your Operations Lean And Clean', 2007.

items.text_en: Well, I have tried to learn as much as possible from prior attempts.
items.text_zh: 嗯，我一直尽量从以前的尝试中学到尽可能多的东西。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: If nothing else, we are committed to failing in a new way.
items.text_zh: 别的先不说，我们至少下定决心要以一种新的方式失败。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: There’s a graveyard of prior attempts, a big graveyard. There’s probably some freshly dug graves just waiting to be filled. Our aspiration is to avoid that destination.
items.text_zh: 以前的尝试有一片墓地，很大一片。可能还有些刚挖好的墓穴正等着被填上。我们的愿望就是避开那个归宿。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: I think we’ve got the risks pretty well characterized. I think we are at least avoiding the mistakes that have been made in the past.
items.text_zh: 我认为我们已经相当清楚地界定了风险。我认为我们至少在避免过去犯过的错误。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: I think the rocket business is quite cyclic. There are a great many peaks and troughs.
items.text_zh: 我认为火箭生意周期性很强，有很多高峰和低谷。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: When thinking about starting a business, I think it’s actually better to start in a trough and come to market in a peak, than the other way around. Frankly, if anything does, and it’s almost cliché, space has a long-term future.
items.text_zh: 考虑创业时，我觉得其实更好的做法是在低谷时起步、在高峰时进入市场，而不是反过来。坦白说，如果说有什么东西——这几乎都成了老生常谈——拥有长期未来，那就是太空。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: I want to be able to make sure that we have enough capital to survive at least three consecutive failures. If you want to make a small fortune in the launch vehicle business, start with a large one.
items.text_zh: 我希望能够确保我们有足够资本撑过至少连续三次失败。如果你想在运载火箭行业赚到一笔小财，那就从一大笔钱开始。
items.source: Lesson #2: Commit To Failing In A New Way', 2007.

items.text_en: The long term ultimate objective – the holy grail – is we would like to help make life multi-planetary.
items.text_zh: 长期的终极目标——圣杯——是我们想帮助让生命遍布多个行星。
items.source: Lesson #3: Make Your Mission Your Holy Grail', 2007.

items.text_en: We got to the moon, but have never done anything better since. I'm disappointed that we have not made more progress since Apollo. I don't even see a plan that says we're going to do better than Apollo to exceed that goal.
items.text_zh: 我们上过月球，但此后从未做过比这更了不起的事。阿波罗之后我们没有取得更多进展，这让我失望。我甚至看不到一个计划说我们要做得比阿波罗更好、超越那个目标。
items.source: Lesson #3: Make Your Mission Your Holy Grail', 2007.

items.text_en: I like to be involved in things that change the world. The Internet did, and space will probably be more responsible for changing the world than anything else. If humanity can expand beyond the Earth, obviously that's where the future is.
items.text_zh: 我喜欢参与改变世界的事情。互联网做到了，而太空可能比任何其他东西都更能改变世界。如果人类能够扩展到地球之外，显然未来就在那里。
items.source: Lesson #3: Make Your Mission Your Holy Grail', 2007.

items.text_en: When Henry Ford made cheap, reliable cars people said, "Nah, what's wrong with a horse?" That was a huge bet he made, and it worked.
items.text_zh: 亨利·福特造出便宜又可靠的汽车时，人们说：“算了吧，马有什么不好？”那是他下的一场豪赌，而且奏效了。
items.source: Lesson #3: Make Your Mission Your Holy Grail', 2007.

items.text_en: It doesn’t do a great deal to advance the goal of humanity. I would pay $20 million not to spend six months in Russia. And besides this, my interest is how do we enable many other people to go to space, not necessarily me, personally.
items.text_zh: 这对推进人类的目标没多大帮助。我愿意花2000万美元，就为了不用在俄罗斯待六个月。除此之外，我感兴趣的是如何让许多其他人也能去太空，而不一定是我本人。
items.source: Lesson #3: Make Your Mission Your Holy Grail', 2007.

items.text_en: Starting and growing a business is as much about the innovation, drive and determination of the people who do it as it is about the product they sell.
items.text_zh: 创办并发展一家企业，既取决于人们卖的产品，也同样取决于做事的人的创新、干劲和决心。
items.source: Lesson #4: Use Innovation To Break Through Your Limitations', 2007.

items.text_en: So even if a fire develops, it can't really attack the particularly vulnerable locations like the pneumatic system or the avionics or the engine bay. We want to be in the situation that even if a fire develops, the rocket just keeps going.
items.text_zh: 所以即使起火，火也无法真正侵袭那些特别脆弱的位置，比如气动系统、航电系统或发动机舱。我们希望做到：即使起火，火箭也照样继续飞。
items.source: Lesson #4: Use Innovation To Break Through Your Limitations', 2007.

items.text_en: A great deal of bargaining power with suppliers. We are never locked in to anyone.
items.text_zh: 面对供应商有很大的议价能力。我们从不被任何一家供应商绑死。
items.source: Lesson #4: Use Innovation To Break Through Your Limitations', 2007.

items.text_en: My approach is simply to seek out very talented people, ensure that the environment at SpaceX is as motivating & enjoyable as possible and establish clear & measurable objectives.
items.text_zh: 我的方法很简单：找出非常有才华的人，确保 SpaceX 的环境尽可能能激励人、让人愉快，并设定清晰且可衡量的目标。
items.source: Lesson #5: Tap Into Today’s Top Talent', 2007.

items.text_en: I think that is a mistake and results in cloudy judgment on important technical issues. They can't tell if something is really good or not, so they just do what everyone else does, assuming it to be the safe bet.
items.text_zh: 我认为那是个错误，会导致在重要技术问题上判断模糊。他们分不清某个东西到底是不是真的好，所以就照着别人做的做，以为那样才稳妥。
items.source: Lesson #5: Tap Into Today’s Top Talent', 2007.

items.text_en: This is the chance to fulfill a dream.
items.text_zh: 这是实现梦想的机会。
items.source: From PayPal To Planetary Success: How Musk Is Changing The World One Company At A Time', 2007.

items.text_en: I’m nauseatingly pro-American. It is where great things are possible.
items.text_zh: 我亲美亲到令人作呕。伟大的事情正是在那里才有可能。
items.source: From PayPal To Planetary Success: How Musk Is Changing The World One Company At A Time', 2007.

items.text_en: As life’s agents, it’s on our shoulders.
items.text_zh: 作为生命的代理人，这责任落在我们肩上。
items.source: From PayPal To Planetary Success: How Musk Is Changing The World One Company At A Time', 2007.

items.text_en: Sooner or later, we must expand life beyond our little blue mud ball--or go extinct.
items.text_zh: 迟早，我们必须把生命扩展到我们这颗小小的蓝色泥球之外——否则就会灭绝。
items.source: 1 October 2008 via Esquire

items.text_en: The heroes of the books I read, The Lord of the Rings and the Foundation series, always felt a duty to save the world.
items.text_zh: 我读过的书里的英雄——《指环王》和《基地》系列——总觉得自己有责任拯救世界。
items.source: 24 August 2009

items.text_en: When something is important enough, you do it even if the odds are not in your favor.
items.text_zh: 当一件事足够重要时，即使胜算不大，你也要去做。
items.source: 18 March 2012 60 Minutes, season 44, episode 26

items.text_en: We need to figure out how to have the things we love, and not destroy the world.
items.text_zh: 我们需要弄清楚，如何既拥有我们热爱的东西，又不毁掉世界。
items.source: 26 March 2012

items.text_en: I'd rather be optimistic and wrong; than pessimistic and right...We have planes, trains, automobiles and boats, ... What if there was a fifth mode?
items.text_zh: 我宁愿乐观而错，也不愿悲观而对……我们有飞机、火车、汽车和船……如果还有第五种交通方式呢？
items.source: 13 July 2012  regarding Hyperloop

items.text_en: One thing that is important is that, if you have a choice between a lower valuation with someone you really like, or higher valuation with someone you have a question mark about, take the lower valuation.
items.text_zh: 有一点很重要：如果你可以选择和一个你真正喜欢的人以较低估值合作，或者和一个你心里没底的人以较高估值合作，那就选较低估值。
items.source: 17 July 2012 during interview with PandoDaily - Fireside Chat With Elon Musk

items.text_en: I would like to die on Mars; just not on impact.
items.text_zh: 我想死在火星上；只是别是撞上去那一刻。
items.source: 12 September 2012

items.text_en: Since our primary competitors [in space launch] are national governments, the enforceability of patents is questionable.
items.text_zh: 由于我们在航天发射领域的主要竞争对手是国家政府，专利的可执行性存疑。
items.source: 19 March 2013

items.text_en: Even if there's a zombie apocalypse, you'll still be able to travel using the Tesla Supercharging system.
items.text_zh: 就算发生丧尸末日，你仍然能靠 Tesla 超级充电系统出行。

items.text_en: I plan to travel to Mars and make it my home...People should be traveling to Mars and doing it in our lifetime.
items.text_zh: 我打算去火星，把那儿当成家……人们应该去火星，而且要在我们这代人有生之年做成这件事。

items.text_en: Everything works in PowerPoint; but if you have the physical item or some demonstration software, that's much more convincing to people than a PowerPoint presentation or a business plan.
items.text_zh: 在 PowerPoint 里什么都能行得通；但如果你有实物，或者有演示软件，那比一份 PowerPoint 演示或商业计划有说服力得多。
items.source: January 23, 2015 Colonizing Mars The Future Belongs to SpaceX and Elon Musk

items.text_en: First, you're going to have to live in transparent domes, but eventually, you can transform Mars into an Earth-like planet. You can warm it up.
items.text_zh: 首先，你得住在透明穹顶里，但最终，你可以把火星改造成类似地球的行星。你可以把它暖起来。
items.source: On the show, Stephen Colbert said he had been trying to decide whether Musk was a superhero or a supervillain, the exchange led him to conclude the latter. University of Colorado atmospheric and ocean sciences professor Brian Toon told the Los Angeles Times: "It seems possible to make it Earthlike, but there's a lot of barriers to overcome [...] Blowing up bombs is not a good one."

items.text_en: [The quick way to warm the planet] Drop thermonuclear weapons over the poles.
items.text_zh: （快速给这颗行星升温的办法）往两极扔热核武器。
items.source: On the show, Stephen Colbert said he had been trying to decide whether Musk was a superhero or a supervillain, the exchange led him to conclude the latter. University of Colorado atmospheric and ocean sciences professor Brian Toon told the Los Angeles Times: "It seems possible to make it Earthlike, but there's a lot of barriers to overcome [...] Blowing up bombs is not a good one."

items.text_en: I'm trying to do useful things.
items.text_zh: 我在努力做有用的事。
items.source: On the show, Stephen Colbert said he had been trying to decide whether Musk was a superhero or a supervillain, the exchange led him to conclude the latter. University of Colorado atmospheric and ocean sciences professor Brian Toon told the Los Angeles Times: "It seems possible to make it Earthlike, but there's a lot of barriers to overcome [...] Blowing up bombs is not a good one."

items.text_en: AI is much more advanced than people realize. ... Humanity's position on this planet depends on its intelligence so if our intelligence is exceeded, it's unlikely that we will remain in charge of the planet.
items.text_zh: AI 比人们意识到的要先进得多。……人类在这个星球上的地位取决于我们的智能，所以如果我们的智能被超越，我们不太可能继续掌管这个星球。
items.source: 25 October 2015 Artificial intelligence: Should we be as terrified as Elon Musk and Bill Gates? in ZDNet

items.text_en: People may outlaw driving cars because it’s too dangerous. You can’t have a person driving a 2-ton death machine.
items.text_zh: 人们可能会因为开车太危险而把它定为非法。你不能让一个人去开一台两吨重的死亡机器。

items.text_en: To be clear, Tesla is strongly in favor of people being allowed to drive their cars and always will be. Hopefully, that is obvious. However, when self-driving cars become safer than human-driven cars, the public may outlaw the latter. Hopefully not.
items.text_zh: 说清楚一点，Tesla 强烈支持允许人们自己开车，而且永远都会如此。希望这一点显而易见。不过，当自动驾驶汽车变得比人类驾驶汽车更安全时，公众可能会禁止后者。希望不会。
items.source: 17 March 2015 Elon Musk Says Human-Driven Cars Could Become Illegal in Huffpost

items.text_en: SpaceX's got 5,000 people. I get a lot of attention, but they are really doing the work.
items.text_zh: SpaceX 有 5000 人。我得到很多关注，但真正干活的是他们。
items.source: 8 April 2016 SpaceX Dragon Headed to the ISS at NASA Post-Launch News Conference

items.text_en: I think we have a duty to maintain the light of consciousness to make sure it continues into the future.
items.text_zh: 我认为我们有责任守护意识之光，确保它延续到未来。
items.source: 8 March 2016

items.text_en: The probability of death is quite high on the first [human] mission [to Mars].
items.text_zh: 第一次（载人）火星任务中，死亡概率相当高。
items.source: 27 September 2016 "Elon Musk's Plan To Colonize Mars Gives Us The Sci-Fi Future We Crave: Now let's see if he can make it reality." Popular Science magazine

items.text_en: It would be an incredible adventure. And life needs to be more than just solving every day problems. You need to wake up and be excited about the future
items.text_zh: 那会是一场不可思议的冒险。生活不能只是解决每天的问题。你需要早上醒来时对未来感到兴奋。
items.source: On "eyeing" for Mars, IAC 2016 meeting, presentation on sustainable Mars colonization.

items.text_en: I can be on my own private island with naked super models, drinking mai tais, but I'm not. I'm in the factory working my ass off, so I don't want to hear about how hard everyone else in the factory works.
items.text_zh: 我本可以在自己的私人岛上，和裸体超模一起喝迈泰，但我没有。我在工厂里拼命干活，所以我不想听别人说工厂里其他人有多辛苦。
items.source: Quoted in "Power Play: Tesla, Elon Musk, and the Bet of the Century" (2021) by Tim Higgins

items.text_en: I think there is a strong humanitarian argument for making life multi-planetary in order to safeguard the existence of humanity in the event that something catastrophic were to happen.
items.text_zh: 我认为，为了让生命成为多行星生命，有一个强有力的人道主义理由：万一发生灾难性事件，可以保住人类的存在。
items.source: 3 October 2017 in DK Smithsonian, Journey: An Illustrated History of Travel, ISBN 978-1-4654-6414-9 (Page 343).

items.text_en: Every person in your company is a vector. Your progress is determined by the sum of all vectors.
items.text_zh: 公司里的每个人都是一个向量。你的进展由所有向量的总和决定。
items.source: 16 October 2017 in LinkedIn: What Elon Musk Taught Me About Growing A Business

items.text_en: Rocket tech applied to a car opens up revolutionary possibilities.
items.text_zh: 把火箭技术用到汽车上，会开启革命性的可能性。
items.source: 19 November 2017 tweet

items.text_en: I love Twitter. How much is it?
items.text_zh: 我爱 Twitter。它卖多少钱？
items.source: 22 December 2017 tweet & tweet

items.text_en: Holy flying fuck, that thing took off!
items.text_zh: 我靠，那玩意儿真飞起来了！
items.source: 12 February 2018 reaction to Falcon Heavy Launch

items.text_en: I don’t get the little ship thing. You can’t show up at Mars in something the size of a rowboat. What if there are Martians? It would be so embarrassing.
items.text_zh: 我不理解那种小飞船的思路。你不能坐着一条划艇大小的东西出现在火星。万一有火星人呢？那也太丢人了。
items.source: 19 February 2018

items.text_en: Guardian is the most insufferable newspaper on planet Earth.
items.text_zh: 《卫报》是地球上最让人受不了的报纸。
items.source: 7 September 2018 e-mail to Guardian, possibly repeated later on a Joe Rogan podcast

items.text_en: im actually cat girl here’s selfie rn
items.text_zh: 我其实是猫娘，这是现在的自拍
items.source: 25 October 2018 tweet

items.text_en: We must pass the great filter!
items.text_zh: 我们必须通过大过滤器！
items.source: 21 June 2020 tweet and TechFilter

items.text_en: We [the United States] will coup whoever we want! Deal with it.
items.text_zh: 我们（美国）想对谁搞政变就搞谁！受着吧。
items.source: 24 July 2020 tweet (archived)

items.text_en: The extreme difficulty of scaling production of new technology is not well understood. It’s 1000% to 10,000% harder than making a few prototypes. The machine that makes the machine is vastly harder than the machine itself.
items.text_zh: 新技术规模化生产的极端难度没有被充分理解。它比造几个原型要难 1000% 到 10000%。造机器的机器，比机器本身难得多。
items.source: 21 September 2020 tweet

items.text_en: All designs are wrong, it's just a matter of how wrong.
items.text_zh: 所有设计都是错的，只是错多少的问题。
items.source: Said while giving tour of Starbase to Tim Dodd (July 30, 2021), https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t705r8ICkRw

items.text_en: Possibly, the most common error of a smart engineer is to optimize something that should not exist.
items.text_zh: 聪明工程师最常见的错误，可能就是去优化一个本不该存在的东西。
items.source: Said while giving tour of Starbase to Tim Dodd (July 30, 2021), https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t705r8ICkRw

items.text_en: If WFP can describe on this Twitter thread exactly how $6B will solve world hunger, I will sell Tesla stock right now and do it.But it must be open source accounting, so the public sees precisely how the money is spent.
items.text_zh: 如果 WFP 能在这个 Twitter 帖子里准确说明 60 亿美元将如何解决全球饥饿问题，我现在就卖掉 Tesla 股票并去做。但必须是开源账目，让公众清楚看到钱到底花在哪儿。
items.source: McSceeney and Pourahmadi are referencing David Beasley's interview on CNN's Connect the World with Becky Anderson

items.text_en: I find history fascinating. There's a lot of incredible things that have been done, good and bad, that they help you understand the nature of civilization and individuals.
items.text_zh: 我觉得历史很迷人。人们做过很多不可思议的事，有好的也有坏的，它们能帮你理解文明和个体的本质。
items.source: "#252 - Elon Musk: SpaceX, Mars, Tesla Autopilot, Self-Driving, Robotics, and AI", on Lex Fridman Podcast (28 December 2021)

items.text_en: We need to expand the scope and scale of consciousness so that we're better able to understand the nature of the universe and understand the meaning of life.
items.text_zh: 我们需要扩展意识的范围和规模，这样我们才能更好地理解宇宙的本质，理解生命的意义。

items.text_en: If you scare people enough, they will demand removal of freedom. This is the path to tyranny.
items.text_zh: 如果你把人吓得够呛，他们就会要求剥夺自由。这是通往暴政的路。

items.text_zh: 我说的是从一开始就不生孩子。问题就在这儿。

items.text_en: A good sign as to whether there is free speech is, "Is someone you don't like allowed to say something you don't like?
items.text_zh: 判断有没有言论自由的一个好标志是：“你讨厌的人是否被允许说你讨厌的话？”
items.source: "Elon Musk talks Twitter, Tesla and how his brain works", TED2022 (April 14, 2022; at 19:39)

items.text_en: This is not a way to make money.... I don't care about the economics at all.
items.text_zh: 这不是赚钱的路子……我根本不在乎经济账。
items.source: "Elon Musk launches hostile bid for Twitter claiming free-speech concerns", CBC (April 14, 2022)

items.text_en: This is just my strong, intuitive sense ... that having a public platform that is maximally trusted and broadly inclusive is extremely important to the future of civilization
items.text_zh: 这只是我强烈的直觉……拥有一个受到最大程度信任、具有广泛包容性的公共平台，对文明的未来极其重要。
items.source: "Elon Musk launches hostile bid for Twitter claiming free-speech concerns", CBC (April 14, 2022)

items.text_zh: 出生率崩塌是文明迄今面临的最大危险。我正在尽我所能帮助应对人口不足危机。

items.text_zh: 火星人口仍然是零！

items.source: "Elon Musk says it’s time for Trump to ‘sail into the sunset’", CNBC (July 12, 2024)

items.source: (October 3, 2022; 7:47pm) tweet

items.text_zh: 我确实受上百万条法律法规约束，其中我遵守了差不多 99.99%。只有当我认為法律违背人民利益时，我才有意见。

items.text_zh: 我只和普京谈过一次，大约是在 18 个月前。谈的是太空。

items.text_zh: 我看到一条路，让 Tesla 的市值超过 Apple 和沙特阿美之和。
